669:
A. Review of Small Wireless Facility Applications. The applicant shall submit its application for small wireless facility permit to the public works department, which shall review the application based on its conformity with this chapter and other applicable regulations, and shall issue a permit on nondiscriminatory terms and conditions subject to the following requirements:
1. Within ten days of receiving an application, the city shall determine and notify the applicant whether the application is complete or incomplete.
2. If the initial application is determined to be complete the city manager or his or her designee shall make its final decision to approve or deny the application within 60 days of the submission of the application.
3. If the initial application is determined to be incomplete, the city shall notify the applicant in writing which information or documents are missing and which provision of the applicable codes requires the submission of the missing information or documents.
a. Upon the receipt of a supplemental submission to complete an application, the city shall make a determination whether the submission is sufficient to render the application complete.
b. If the initial application is rendered complete by the supplemental submission, the city shall make its final decision to approve or deny the application within 60 days of the supplemental submission.
c. If city determines the supplemental submission does not render the application complete, the city shall notify the applicant which information or documents need to be submitted to render the application complete.
d. When any supplemental submissions are deemed by the city as insufficient to render the application complete, the city's obligation to make a final decision shall be tolled from the day after the date of the notice of deficiency until such time as the applicant submits all the documents and information identified as necessary to render the application complete.
4. The city shall notify the applicant in writing of its final decision, and if the application is denied the city shall specify the basis for denial and, where applicable, shall cite to the specific provisions of this chapter or to the applicable federal, state, or local codes.
5. Notwithstanding the initial denial, the applicant may cure any deficiencies identified by the city if curable within 30 days of the denial without paying an additional application fee, provided the city shall approve or deny the revised application within ten days of receipt of the amended application.
6. An applicant seeking to construct, modify or replace a network of small wireless facilities may, at the applicant's discretion, file a consolidated application for up to five small wireless facilities and receive a single permit for such multiple small wireless facilities, unless WIP obtains permission in advance from the public works department to include more than five small wireless facilities in an application; provided, however, the denial of one or more small wireless facilities in a consolidated application shall not delay processing of any other small wireless facilities in the same consolidated application.
B. Appeal.
1. Any applicant who wishes to appeal the denial or revocation of a permit shall, within ten days of the date of the notice of an adverse determination, submit a notice of appeal to the city clerk.
2. The notice of appeal shall be addressed to the council and shall specify the subject matter of the appeal, the date of any original and amended application or requests, the date of the adverse decision (or receipt of notice thereof), the basis of the appeal, the action requested of the council, and the name and address of the applicant.
3. The clerk shall place the appeal on the agenda of the next regular council meeting occurring not less than five nor more than 45 days after receipt of the application for council action.
4. Once the city clerk has scheduled an appeal before the city council, at the time and date set therefor, the council shall receive all relevant testimony and evidence from the applicant, from interested parties and from city staff. The mayor, the mayor pro tem or the presiding officer shall preside over the appeal hearing and may set appropriate time limits for the presentation of evidence. The mayor and city council shall not be bound by the traditional rules of evidence in hearings conducted under this chapter. Rules of evidence as applied in an administrative hearing shall apply. The city council may vote to sustain, over-rule or modify the action complained of. The action of the city council shall be final, and any appeal of their decision shall be to superior court.
C. Review of Eligible Facilities Requests. Nothing in this chapter is intended to supersede or conflict with applications for eligible facilities requests according to the procedures established under Section 5-4, streets and sidewalks.
(Ord. No. 8001, 1/10/2018, § 1; Ord. No. 8124, 12/11/2019, § 1)
670:
A. All small wireless facilities shall require an attachment agreement or other authorization for placement on the pole or wireless support structure and shall be subject to the following requirements, except that any small wireless facility proposed to be located in a protected area, as identified on the map described in Subsection B., shall comply with the requirements of that section to the extent they differ from the requirement below:
1. Installations in/on utility poles not located within protected areas shall be limited to in-line tangent poles without transformers and those classified as secondary service poles.
2. To the greatest extent practical, antennas shall not be perceptible by an average person from 250 feet away; if a dispute arises as to this paragraph, the public works director will make the final determination as to compliance with this paragraph. All location decisions shall be addressed in a nondiscriminatory manner and consistent with applicable law.
3. Small wireless facility installations on all poles shall utilize a concealed design, with all cabling being inside a hollow pole or otherwise hidden from view without banding or external conduit or panduit.
4. All radios, network equipment and batteries will be enclosed inside the pole or on the pole inside a concealment device approved by the city public works department.
5. All SWF shall be designed in a manner that does not endanger public safety or impede traffic flow on roads and sidewalks.
6. Any new poles installed shall not leach any volatile organic compounds or toxic materials.
7. Any new poles installed should be constructed in a manner to avoid unsightly rust and corrosion. The finish on the pole should conform to city standards, including selection of color, finish method, such as "baked on" or color that is tightly integrated into the material composition of the pole to prevent color fading or erosion or peeling of paint from the exterior of the pole.
8. Any SWF placed on a city-owned pole shall not interfere with or block any banners or other attachments owned by the city. The small wireless facility shall be aesthetically compatible with the surrounding area through application of camouflage and concealment design techniques.
9. Any new, modified, or replacement pole or wireless support structure installed in the rights-of-way located outside of a protected area shall not exceed five feet above the tallest pre-existing poles or wireless support structures within 200 feet of the proposed new wireless facility, located on the same side of the street and within the same right-of-way, except that no pole shall exceed 65 feet above ground level (AGL).
10. Any poles located in protected areas or streetscaped corridors, shall be consistent in height with the other decorative poles located therein. The city shall not allow new poles in any protected area without a variance from city council, which may only be granted upon a showing by the WIP that service to the area would be effectively prohibited without the installation of a new pole, and any replacement poles must match the height of the existing pole it replaces.
11. Applicant shall comply with all requirements set forth in the city's underground utility ordinance. The provisions of the city's underground utility ordinance shall be applied in a manner consistent with its application other utility providers that use the city's rights-of-way and in such a way that does not effectively prohibit service within the area of the proposed facility.
12. Any small wireless facilities proposed to be located within 250 feet of another small wireless facility shall be collocated with other small wireless facilities or neutrally hosted, unless applicant provides sufficient evidence that coverage and capacity needs cannot be met using collocated or neutrally hosted wireless attachments; any small wireless facilities shall be designed and constructed in a manner that allows other competing wireless infrastructure providers and carriers to be collocated on/in the same pole or placed on/in nearby poles. All location decisions shall be addressed in a nondiscriminatory manner and consistent with applicable law. It is the express intent of this chapter that in areas where one WIP has installed SWF, all providers and carriers be shall permitted to install SWF in the same area consistent with the Telecommunications Act of 1996, including 47 U.S. Code § 224, and other applicable provisions. To the extent such collocation or nearby placement is not feasible in certain rights-of-way, all wireless infrastructure providers shall be prohibited from installing SWF in that area of the right-of-way, and the public works department has authority to deny or revoke any permits for SWF in that area if it is shown that WIP are being blocked by competing WIP from locating there. As SWF technology continues to develop and smaller and more concealed designs are available, the city may review permits and require that WIP upgrade older SWF so that more WIP may collocate and/or decrease the footprint of SWF in the rights-of-way.
B. Protected Areas.
1. The city has invested significant capital and regulatory efforts over many years to promote economic and community development, support the preservation of historic and natural resources, and remedy potential blight through redevelopment initiatives. In keeping with this effort to protect these significant investments in sensitive areas, the city council may designate certain areas of the city in which in which streetscaping, historic preservation, redevelopment efforts, or other zoning and land use considerations require the design and construction of small wireless facilities in a manner that conforms to the existing aesthetic and structural schemes. The regulations adopted to protect these areas will be applied in a manner consistent with the city's regulation of other utility providers that use the city's rights-of-way and in such a way that does not effectively prohibit service within these areas.
2. The protected areas are identified on the protected area maps included with this chapter and adopted concurrently herewith. The city council may update the protected area maps as additional areas within the city are designated as protected areas. The public works department shall maintain a corresponding list of city-approved pole(s) for each protected area identified on the map.
3. Small wireless facilities located in protected areas with existing decorative poles shall use poles that conform to the height and aesthetics of the existing decorative poles. The public works department shall maintain a list of city-approved poles for each protected area and a list of design specifications for SWF placed in each protected area, including height limits, equipment placement, and concealment requirements.
4. Any poles located in protected areas or streetscaped corridors shall be consistent in height with the other decorative poles located therein. The city shall not allow new poles in any protected area without a variance from city council which may only be granted upon a showing by the WIP that service to the area would be effectively prohibited without the installation of a new pole, and any replacement poles must match the height of the existing pole it replaces.
5. Pole-mounted cabinets approved by the city in protected areas shall conform to the design and placement specifications determined by the public works department for each protected area and cabinets on the ground are prohibited altogether in protected areas.
6. Where the city has or hereafter decides to relocate utility facilities underground or replace poles with decorative poles, the city shall designate such area as a protected area and shall work with the wireless infrastructure provider to accommodate placement of SWF on city-approved poles within that area provided the SWF conform to poles used in the area. In order to place to place any SWF on a pole that has not been approved by the city for use in the protected area, WIP must seek a variance from the city council, which shall only be granted upon a showing that service to the area would be effectively prohibited without the use of the non-approved pole.
(Ord. No. 8001, 1/10/2018, § 1; Ord. No. 8124, 12/11/2019, § 1)
671:
A. Authority Granted: No Property Right or Other Interest Created. A permit from the city authorizes an applicant to undertake only certain activities in accordance with this chapter and does not create a property right or grant any authority whatsoever to the applicant to impinge upon the rights of others who may already have an interest in the rights-of-way.
B. Duration. Unless construction has actually begun and is diligently pursued to completion at that point, no permit for construction issued under this chapter shall be valid for a period longer than 12 months unless both city and applicant agree to a reasonable extension and all required fees are paid for the term regardless of construction.
C. Public Safety and Traffic. Construction and maintenance of SWF shall be performed in a manner that does not endanger public safety and that minimizes interference with traffic flow. Where permittee must disrupt traffic flow, appropriate safety and traffic flow measures shall be employed to safeguard against accidents and keep traffic moving in an efficient manner.
D. Condition of Right-of-Way. Upon completion of any construction or maintenance of its small wireless facilities, the wireless infrastructure provider must return the surface of the city's right-of-way to its prior condition, including any sidewalks, curbing, paving, landscaping or other improvements in place prior to the construction. WIP shall not leave sidewalks in an uneven condition and shall use similar materials and construction in its repair of the right-of-way such that the appearance of the improvements is substantially identical to its prior condition. If the right-of-way is not returned to a substantially identical condition after construction or maintenance activities, the city may, in its sole discretion, request the WIP to make the appropriate repairs within five days of receiving notice from the city. If the repairs are not made by the WIP within said time, the city may perform the repairs on its own and require reimbursement of any expenses associated therewith. When such repairs are made by the city, written notice shall be sent requesting reimbursement upon completion of the repairs, and WIP shall have 30 days to reimburse such expenses from the sending of the notice.
E. Construction and Maintenance Exclusions. The city retains the authority to exclude certain days, holidays and special events periods during which the wireless infrastructure provider may not perform construction or maintenance activities on its small wireless facilities and must be out of the rights-of-way. The public works department may also require that WIP and their agents not perform construction or maintenance work during certain times of the day in order to lessen the impact on traffic or otherwise address safety concerns. Such times shall be as approved by the city council or the public works director. Prior to commencing construction or maintenance, permittee or its agent must verify that its planned work does not fall into an excluded time period.
F. Compliance with ADA. Any small wireless facilities or associated construction and maintenance activities must comply with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (Section 504) (29 U.S.C. § 794) and Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA) (42 U.S.C. §§ 12131—12164). The city shall not be liable for any small wireless facilities or any actions of the WIP which violate the ADA. If at any time the city determines the right-of-way is not in compliance due to the actions or facilities of WIP, the city may, in its sole discretion, request the WIP to make the appropriate repairs within five days of sending of the notice from the city. If the repairs are not made by the WIP, the city may perform the repairs on its own and require reimbursement of any expenses associated therewith. When such repairs are made by the city, written notice shall be sent requesting reimbursement upon completion of the repairs, and WIP shall have 30 days to reimburse such expenses from the sending of the notice.

A. General Relocation Policy.
1. In the interest of the public health, safety and welfare, consistent with the city's ordinances and master plans, and in the reasonable exercise of its police powers, the city may make or cause to be made improvements, repairs, or replacements of the public facilities located on public rights-of-way. Such construction activity may require adjustment or relocation of installations of public utilities, and small wireless facilities owned and maintained by wireless service providers. The city deems the right of public utilities to use public rights-of-way to be permissive and subordinate to the reasonable exercise of the city's police power. Thus, the cost of relocating a small wireless facility installation when the city reasonably exercises its police power shall be borne by the wireless infrastructure provider. In such instances, the city shall work in good faith with the wireless providers to identify and provide suitable alternative locations for the placement of the removed wireless facilities if available and consistent with this chapter. The city's relocation policy will be applied in a manner consistent with the city's relocation of other utility providers that use the city's rights-of-way and in such a way that does not effectively prohibit service within these area of the project requiring relocation.
2. Whenever the city determines that relocation of a SWF is necessary under this provision, the city shall give WIP 60 days' notice within which to relocate or otherwise remove the SWF. Should the wireless infrastructure provider not relocate as directed by the city, the city may disconnect and remove the wireless attachment, ancillary equipment or the entire small wireless facility at the wireless infrastructure provider's expense. When such removal is performed by the city, written notice shall be sent requesting reimbursement after completion of the removal, and WIP shall have 30 days to reimburse such expenses after the sending of the notice. Failure to timely reimburse shall terminate right to be in city ROW.
B. Emergency Removal or Relocation of Facilities. The city retains the right to cut or move or disconnect any small wireless facility located within its rights-of-way as the city, in its sole discretion, may determine to be necessary, appropriate, or useful in response to any public health or safety emergency. If circumstances permit, the city shall notify the wireless infrastructure provider and provide it an opportunity to move its own small wireless facility, prior to the city cutting or removing such facility and the city shall notify the wireless infrastructure provider after cutting or removing the small wireless facility. The city shall not be liable for any damages to small wireless facilities or other infrastructure that is cut or removed during such emergencies. When such removal is performed by the city, written notice shall be sent requesting reimbursement after completion of the removal, and WIP shall have 30 days to reimburse such expenses after the sending of the notice.

For the purpose of this chapter, the following terms, phrases, words, and their derivations shall have the meaning given herein.
A. "Bulk container" shall mean a two, two and one-half, three, four, six, or eight cubic yard metal container.
B. "Commercial handbill" shall mean any printed or written matter, any sample or device, circular, leaflet, pamphlet, paper, booklet, or any other printed or otherwise reproduced original or copies of any matter of literature which:
1. Advertises for sale any merchandise, product, commodity, service, business, opportunity or thing;
2. Directs attention to any business or mercantile or commercial establishment or other activity, for the purpose of either directly or indirectly promoting the interest thereof by sales; or
3. Directs attention to or advertises any meeting, theatrical performance, exhibition, or event of any kind, for which an admission fee is charged, or a collection is taken; or
4. While containing reading matter other than advertising matter, is predominately and essentially an advertisement, and is distributed or circulated for advertising purposes or for the private benefit and gain of any person so engaged as advertise or distributor.
C. "Construction wastes" shall mean scrap lumber, pipe, plaster, cement, and other construction materials from new or remodeled structures.
D. "Demolition wastes" shall mean lumber, pipes, brick masonry, and other construction materials from razed buildings and other structures.
E. "Food service establishments" means and includes establishments for the preparation and serving of meals, lunches, short orders, sandwiches, frozen desserts, or other edible products. This term includes, but is not limited to, restaurants, coffee shops, cafeterias, short order cafes, luncheonettes, taverns, lunchrooms, places manufacturing, wholesaling, or retailing sandwiches or salads, soda fountains, institutions, both public and private, food carts, itinerant restaurants, industrial cafeterias, school cafeterias, catering establishments, food vending machines and vehicles and operations connected therewith, and similar facilities by whatever name called.
F. "Garbage" shall mean any putrescible or nonputrescible, organic or inorganic, combustible, or noncombustible wastes, wastes from the preparation, cooking and serving of foods or liquids, market wastes, wastes from the handling and storage of produce, and those items of solid wastes normally generated as household refuse which can be properly and safely fitted into an approved solid waste container. The term garbage may include, but is not limited to, the following kinds of materials:
1. Combustible materials such as wax cartons, paper, paper and cardboard boxes, cellophane wrapper, excelsior, and any other small combustible items.
2. Noncombustible materials such as metal cans, glass, glass containers, cookware, and any other small noncombustible items.
G. "Individual nondisposable containers" shall mean a watertight receptacle or open top "recycling" bin of a solid or durable grade metal, plastic or rubber, or other such material as may be approved by the public works director.
H. "Private premises" shall mean any dwelling house, building, or other structure, designed or used either wholly or in part for private residential purposes, whether inhabited or vacant and may include any yard, grounds, walk, driveway, porch, steps, vestibule, or mailbox belonging or appurtenant to such dwelling, house building or other structure.
I. "The public works director" shall mean the director of public works department or an authorized agent thereof.
J. "Solid waste" or "refuse" as used in this chapter shall include, but shall not be limited to, the following types of wastes: Garbage, rubbish, trash, demolition wastes, construction wastes, and special wastes.
K. "Special wastes" shall mean hazardous solids and liquids, explosives, pathological wastes, and radioactive materials.
L. "Trash" is defined to mean any nonputrescible, large combustible or noncombustible item of solid waste generated as household refuse. The term trash may include, but is not limited to, the following kinds of materials:
1. "Combustible materials" such as tied and bundled paper and cardboard, carpet, bedding, wood furniture, and other large combustible items.
2. "Noncombustible materials" such as large metals, empty paint cans, metal furniture, large appliances, garden tools, lawn decorations, hose, and any other large noncombustible items.
M. "Weed" shall mean any useless, troublesome, and obnoxious plant that grows profusely.
N. "Yard trimmings" is defined to mean any putrescible, combustible, or noncombustible item of solid waste generated by the cutting action of an owner or occupant from around the premises. The term yard trimmings may include, but is not limited to, the following kinds of materials:
O. "Materials" such as tree branches, logs, leaves, pine needles, grass clippings and brush.

A. Residential Uses.
1. Single-family and two-family structures. Each household shall be provided with individual nondisposable containers, by the public works department, to adequately and properly store all garbage, as defined herein, until removed by the public works department. The use of nondisposable containers shall be governed by the specifications established in this chapter. Nondisposable containers shall, at all times, be protected from weather conditions, animals, children, and objects that may cause the wastes of the container to be littered, if stored outside. No items shall be placed within durable plastic containers that could cause injury to collection personnel. Individual nondisposable garbage containers shall be stored or be accessible at the rear or side of each household, on the real property of the property owner or account holder, and shall be placed curbside only, after 5:00 p.m. the night before the scheduled collection day, and removed from curbside by the end of the day of collection, and returned to the rear or side of each household on the real property of the property owner or account holder. Items placed in nondisposable containers should be properly bagged to ensure removal when collected. Allowances for the back door pickup will be granted by the public works department if the resident has mobility issues and submits the proper form.
2. The public works department will provide regular collection services for household garbage, recyclable material, and yard trimmings of less than 200 cubic feet. Collection services will be provided on a weekly basis. Residents must contact the public works department sanitation division to request collection of trash items. Collection of bulk trash and recyclable items by the public works department will be subject to an additional service charge included on the resident's utility bill. The service charge will be in accordance with the fee schedule approved by the mayor and city council.
3. Yard trimmings and trash as defined herein, shall be placed adjacent to the curb of the property from which it originates for collection, but in no case shall it be placed in such a position as to obstruct the sidewalk, the gutter, the free movement of traffic, or prohibit the collection with collection equipment. All yard trimmings and trash stored in disposable containers shall be securely sealed for curbside collection. 681:
Following are specifications and requirements for the handling of solid waste and the location, screening, and maintenance requirements of nondisposable and bulk containers.
A. Individual Nondisposable Containers in General.
1. Individual nondisposable solid waste containers that have deteriorated to the extent of having sharp or jagged edges, capable of causing injury to collection personnel, or to such an extent that the lid will not fit tightly and securely, or that it is not watertight, shall be replaced at the discretion of the public works director. All owners or occupants of single-family and two-family structures shall place items in plastic bags as liners for individual nondisposable containers.
2. Individual nondisposable solid waste containers shall be stored at the rear of each residence, business, or industry unless an alternative location is authorized by the public works director. Location of a bulk container on city rights-of-way is prohibited unless a permit is granted by the public works director. All garbage, as described herein, shall be brought to the curb only after 5:00 p.m. the night before the scheduled day of collection, and removed from curbside by the end of the day of collection. All other types of solid waste, as defined herein, shall be placed accessible from the curb in front of the property from which it originates for collection, but in no case shall it be placed in such a position as to obstruct the sidewalk, the gutter, the free movement of traffic, or prohibit the collection with collection equipment. Containers shall be covered tightly, and disposable containers sealed for curbside collection. All empty paper cartons or cardboard boxes deposited alongside the curb or in containers shall be broken down, flattened, and tied into manageable bundles.
3. No item of trash, as defined herein, shall be collected by the public works department by regularly scheduled collection. Arrangements for collections of this type shall be made between the owner or occupant of the premises and the public works department. Those waste items which are too large or heavy to be safely handled by the equipment or personnel of the public works department must be collected and transported for disposal by the owner or occupant. An owner or occupant desiring unscheduled collection shall notify the director of the public works department, or his designee, three working days prior to the date of desired collection. The public works department is authorized to charge a fee as established by the mayor and city council per pickup based upon the request of an owner or occupant.
4. Trash or yard trimmings shall be placed at a curbside location adjacent to the originating property prior to 7:00 a.m. on the day of expected removal, but in no case shall it be placed in such a position as to obstruct the sidewalk, gutter, free movement of traffic, or prohibit the collection with collection equipment. Trash or yard trimmings placed at a curbside location, shall at all times, be protected from weather conditions, animals, children, and objects that may cause the waste to be littered.
5. Refrigerators and freezers shall have doors removed before placing at curbside for collection.
6. All leaves, grass clippings, pine needles, and similar yard trimmings shall be placed in reusable nondisposable rigid containers or compostable brown paper bags and deposited at a curbside location adjacent to the originating property, but in no case shall it be placed in such a position as to obstruct the sidewalks, the gutter, er the free movement of traffic, or prohibit the collection with collection equipment. All branches, limbs, and shrubbery shall be cut in lengths of six feet or less, and no single piece shall exceed four inches in diameter and weigh no more than 100 pounds.
7. All commercial tree and shrubbery firms, and clearing, grading, and building contractors shall be responsible for the collection and disposal of their own debris.
8. In order to maintain an orderly collection schedule, the director of the public works department may, at his or her discretion, limit the amount of trash or yard trimmings exceeding the weight requirement of 1,000 pounds collected at any one location to one truckload per scheduled collection.
B. Individual Nondisposable Containers; Specifications. Individual nondisposable containers shall be a watertight receptacle and be equipped with suitable handles on the outside and a tight fitting cover of like material equipped with a handle.
C. Bulk Containers; Specifications.
1. Bulk solid waste containers shall be constructed of a solid grade metal of either a two, two and one-half, three, four, six, or eight cubic yard capacity equipped with lids, drains, and drain plugs.
2. Bulk containers shall be accessible to garbage collection vehicles at all times.
3. Bulk containers shall be kept in a sanitary condition.
4. Bulk doors and lids shall be secured at all times.
